# Figure 2

## Getting the data

Processed data are deposited at ArrayExpress, genome assemblies at ENA:

| Data | Accession |
|---|---|
| Single-nucleus RNA-seq | `E-MTAB-17757` |
| Single-nucleus ATAC-seq | `E-MTAB-17776` |
| Genome assemblies | `PRJEB115767` |

Everything except the single-nucleus atlases is committed in this repository
under `data/reference/`: orthology maps, TF lists, SAMap scores, gene-to-GO
maps, TF activity, the differential expression tables and the SCENIC+ output.

Only the atlases need downloading. Put them in one folder and point
`DATA_DIR` at it; the files are used exactly as ArrayExpress delivers them, so
nothing needs renaming.

```
<DATA_DIR>/
`-- snRNA/
    `-- seurat/                                  E-MTAB-17757
        |-- BifurcaAtlas.rds
        |-- BrachiAtlas.rds
        |-- FormosaAtlas.rds
        |-- GracilisAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant.rds
        |-- GracilisAtlas_pregnant.rds
        |-- InfansAtlas.rds
        |-- PhallocerusAtlas.rds
        |-- PictaAtlas.rds
        |-- ProlificaAtlas.rds
        |-- TurneriAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant_juvenile.rds
        `-- TurneriAtlas_pregnant.rds
```

Panels use the combined atlas for *P. gracilis* and *P. turneri* unless stated
otherwise; Figure 1B uses the pregnant-only *P. turneri* atlas.

Every atlas carries a `cell_type` column, which the scripts use rather than
per-species cluster numbers.

## Panels in this file

| Panel | Chunk | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 2B | `fig2b` | SAMap correlation heatmap, all nine poeciliids |
| 2D | `fig2d` | *P. turneri* cell-type composition, adult against juvenile |
| 2E | `fig2e` | *P. gracilis* cell-type composition, pregnant against non-pregnant |

The cluster set used below is the same one behind Supplementary Figure 4A, which
re-plots it as a dendrogram.

```{r knitr-setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", dev = "png", dpi = 300)
```

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## PURPOSE : Set the two paths every chunk below reads from, and load packages.
## PRODUCES: DATA_DIR, REF_DIR
## QUESTION: none - configuration only.

DATA_DIR <- "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"   # master folder described above
REF_DIR  <- "../data/reference"             # reference tables, committed in this repo

stopifnot(dir.exists(DATA_DIR), dir.exists(REF_DIR))

## The atlases are read under the names ArrayExpress delivers, so nothing needs
## renaming after download.
ATLAS <- c(bifurca   = "BifurcaAtlas.rds",
           brachi    = "BrachiAtlas.rds",
           formosa   = "FormosaAtlas.rds",
           gracilis  = "GracilisAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant.rds",
           infans    = "InfansAtlas.rds",
           phallo    = "PhallocerusAtlas.rds",
           picta     = "PictaAtlas.rds",
           prolifica = "ProlificaAtlas.rds",
           turneri   = "TurneriAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant_juvenile.rds")

ATLAS_PREGNANT <- c(gracilis = "GracilisAtlas_pregnant.rds",
                    turneri  = "TurneriAtlas_pregnant.rds")

atlas_path <- function(sp, pregnant = FALSE)
  file.path(DATA_DIR, "snRNA", "seurat",
            if (pregnant) ATLAS_PREGNANT[[sp]] else ATLAS[[sp]])


suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(viridis)
  library(pheatmap)
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(Seurat)
})
```

```{r samap-matrix}
## PURPOSE : Read the pairwise SAMap mapping scores for all nine poeciliids.
## PRODUCES: mat - a cluster x cluster matrix of SAMap scores
## QUESTION: how transcriptionally similar is each cell cluster to each cluster
##           in every other species?

mat <- as.matrix(read.csv(
  file.path(REF_DIR, "rna", "SAMap", "MappingValues_Pairwise_samap.txt"),
  row.names = 1))

## The matrix is labelled <two-letter species>_<cluster number>. The cleaned
## atlases no longer carry that clustering, so the cluster -> cell type key is
## committed alongside the matrix; see its `source` column for how each was set.
CLUSTER_KEY <- read.csv(file.path(REF_DIR, "rna", "SAMap", "cluster_cell_types.csv"))
cell_type_of <- setNames(CLUSTER_KEY$cell_type, CLUSTER_KEY$label)

## a species may have several clusters of one type, so the cluster id is kept in
## the label to keep rows distinguishable and traceable back to the matrix
pretty_label <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(cell_type_of[x]), x,
                                   sprintf("%s (%s)", cell_type_of[x], x))

dim(mat)
```

```{r fig2b, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 9}
## PURPOSE : Figure 2B - SAMap scores between the retained ovarian clusters of
##           all nine poeciliids, clustered on correlation distance.
## PRODUCES: the heatmap, printed in the document
## QUESTION: do homologous ovarian cell types map to one another across the whole
##           family, including the non-placental species?

## clusters retained after QC, one block per species
samap_clusters <- c(
  "bi_0","bi_2","bi_3","bi_6","bi_7","bi_8","bi_12","bi_19",
  "pr_1","pr_3","pr_5","pr_6","pr_8","pr_9","pr_10","pr_12","pr_17",
  "tu_1","tu_2","tu_3","tu_4","tu_5","tu_9","tu_10","tu_11","tu_12",
  "fo_0","fo_1","fo_2","fo_5","fo_6","fo_7","fo_8","fo_9","fo_11",
  "pi_1","pi_2","pi_3","pi_4","pi_5","pi_6","pi_7",
  "in_0","in_2","in_3","in_4","in_5","in_6","in_7","in_12",
  "gr_0","gr_2","gr_3","gr_4","gr_5","gr_7","gr_10","gr_11","gr_14",
  "br_0","br_1","br_3","br_5","br_6","br_7","br_9","br_11","br_13","br_14")

## the matrix is square, so the same labels index rows and columns;
## zebrafish is the outgroup used to build the scores, not a comparison
## subset in the matrix's own order, as Diego's script does
keep <- setdiff(rownames(mat)[rownames(mat) %in% samap_clusters],
                grep("^ze_", rownames(mat), value = TRUE))
samap_mat <- mat[keep, keep]

## a cluster maps to itself perfectly by definition
diag(samap_mat) <- 1

rownames(samap_mat) <- colnames(samap_mat) <- pretty_label(rownames(samap_mat))

## the published panel is greyscale, white at 0 and black at 1
pheatmap(t(samap_mat),
         color                    = colorRampPalette(c("white", "black"))(100),
         clustering_distance_rows = "correlation",
         clustering_distance_cols = "correlation",
         clustering_method        = "ward.D2",
         main                     = "SAMap scores across nine poeciliids",
         angle_col                = 45,
         fontsize = 8, fontsize_row = 8, fontsize_col = 6,
         border_color             = NA)
```

```{r fig2d-2e-data}
## PURPOSE : For each cell type, what share of its nuclei came from each stage.
## PRODUCES: stage_df - cell type x stage proportions for both species
## QUESTION: none - shared input for the two panels below.

## P. turneri is split adult against juvenile, with pregnant and non-pregnant
## pooled into adult; P. gracilis is split pregnant against non-pregnant.
SPLIT <- list(
  turneri  = list(levels = c("Adult", "Juvenile"),
                  rule = function(s) ifelse(grepl("juvenile", s, ignore.case = TRUE),
                                            "Juvenile", "Adult")),
  gracilis = list(levels = c("Pregnant", "Non-Pregnant"),
                  rule = function(s) ifelse(grepl("non", s, ignore.case = TRUE),
                                            "Non-Pregnant", "Pregnant"))
)

stage_for <- function(sp) {
  obj <- readRDS(atlas_path(sp))
  md  <- obj@meta.data
  if (!"Sample_status" %in% names(md))
    stop(sp, ": no Sample_status column. Columns: ", paste(names(md), collapse = ", "))
  message(sp, " Sample_status values: ",
          paste(sort(unique(as.character(md$Sample_status))), collapse = ", "))

  g <- SPLIT[[sp]]
  md |>
    mutate(stage     = factor(g$rule(as.character(Sample_status)), levels = g$levels),
           cell_type = as.character(cell_type)) |>
    filter(!is.na(stage), !is.na(cell_type)) |>
    count(cell_type, stage) |>
    group_by(cell_type) |>
    mutate(proportion = n / sum(n)) |>      # within each cell type, so bars reach 100%
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(species = sp)
}

stage_df <- bind_rows(lapply(c("turneri", "gracilis"), stage_for))

## Seurat's default two-colour palette: ggplot's hue scale for n = 2
SEURAT_TWO <- scales::hue_pal()(2)          # "#F8766D" red, "#00BFC4" teal

## the late follicle cell is the panel's subject, so it leads; the rest follow
## in decreasing size
stage_bars <- function(sp) {
  d <- filter(stage_df, species == sp)
  ord <- d |> group_by(cell_type) |> summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(desc(n)) |> pull(cell_type)
  ord <- c(intersect("Late follicle cell", ord), setdiff(ord, "Late follicle cell"))

  ggplot(mutate(d, cell_type = factor(cell_type, levels = ord)),
         aes(cell_type, proportion, fill = stage)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(SEURAT_TWO, SPLIT[[sp]]$levels), name = "Stage") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
          legend.position = "right")
}
```

```{r fig2d, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
## PURPOSE : Figure 2D - P. turneri composition, adult against juvenile.
## PRODUCES: the stacked bars, printed in the document
## QUESTION: which cell types are present only once the ovary is adult?

stage_bars("turneri")
```

```{r fig2e, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
## PURPOSE : Figure 2E - P. gracilis composition, pregnant against non-pregnant.
## PRODUCES: the stacked bars, printed in the document
## QUESTION: which cell types change in proportion with pregnancy?

stage_bars("gracilis")
```
